timeline.name: Vibrolux Reverb
timeline.voice: Two 6L6s and two tens with the full black-panel reverb and tremolo.
timeline.story: Two 6L6s and two ten-inch speakers in a cabinet about 25 inches wide, with the same reverb and optical tremolo setup as the bigger black-panel combos. Both channels have Volume, Treble, Bass and a Bright switch, and the Vibrato channel adds Reverb, Speed and Intensity. There’s no Middle knob; a fixed 6.8K resistor sits where it would go. A 12AT7 drives the reverb tank through its own small transformer, and half a 7025 brings the signal back. The tremolo is a lamp and a light-sensitive resistor in a sealed package, and it only works on the Vibrato channel. Fender introduced it in 1964 and kept it in black until 1967.
timeline.ratingNote: Catalog row 68, 35 W. Circuit read from Fender drawing AA964 (J-FD), a later print; no AA864 drawing was found (Q32). Cabinet 18 × 25 × 9.5 in from Mojotone; one dealer measures 17.75 × 24.5 × 9.5 in. Both first-year amps photographed have the raised grille logo (Q33).

parts.label: Tube-driven spring reverb
parts.title: The reverb has its own tube and transformer.
parts.body: The reverb isn’t a passive add-on. Half a 12AT7 drives the spring tank through a small transformer, and half a 7025 picks up the return. The Reverb knob is a 100K pot blending the wet signal back in through a .003 µF cap.
parts.listen: Because the tank is driven hard, a little Reverb goes a long way, and past halfway it gets splashy fast.
parts.together: The tank plugs into the RCA jacks marked Reverb Output and Reverb Input on the back. The reverb is on the Vibrato channel only.
parts.detail: How the reverb sounds is player consensus, not a measurement.
sources: Fender "Vibrolux Reverb-Amp AA964" schematic, drawing J-FD
Mojotone field guide: Blackface Vibrolux Reverb

parts.label: Optical tremolo
parts.title: The tremolo is a lamp and a light sensor.
parts.body: Half a 12AX7 runs as an oscillator, with the Speed control a 3M pot. The oscillator flashes a small lamp sealed next to a light-dependent resistor, and that resistor pulls the Vibrato channel’s signal up and down. Intensity is a 50K pot.
parts.listen: It only works on the Vibrato channel. Plug into Normal and the Speed and Intensity knobs do nothing.
parts.together: The oscillator, lamp and photocell are the same plan the drawing for the black-panel Pro Reverb shows.
parts.detail: The sealed lamp package is drawn as a block; its exact part isn’t named on this print.
sources: Fender "Vibrolux Reverb-Amp AA964" schematic, drawing J-FD

parts.label: Fixed middle resistor
parts.title: There’s a Middle setting, you just can’t turn it.
parts.body: Each channel’s tone stack is a 250K Treble and a 250K Bass with a fixed 6.8K resistor at the bottom, where a Middle pot would go on a Twin or Super Reverb.
parts.listen: A 6.8K resistor is a fairly low middle setting, so the mids are pulled back compared with a Middle pot turned up.
parts.together: The stack uses a 250 pF treble cap and .1 µF and .047 µF caps.
parts.detail: The comparison to other models is ours.
sources: Fender "Vibrolux Reverb-Amp AA964" schematic, drawing J-FD

parts.label: Bright switch
parts.title: The Bright switch is a 120 pF cap.
parts.body: Each channel has a Bright switch that puts a 120 pF cap across its 1M Volume pot.
parts.listen: Like any bright cap on a volume pot, it’s strongest with the Volume low and fades as you turn up.
parts.together: Both channels start in a 7025, one per channel.
sources: Fender "Vibrolux Reverb-Amp AA964" schematic, drawing J-FD

parts.label: Two 6L6s with adjustable bias
parts.title: Two 6L6GCs and a bias you can set.
parts.body: Two 6L6GC output tubes run on fixed bias of about -42 V, with a 10K pot to adjust it. A 12AT7 long-tailed pair drives them, and feedback comes back through an 820 Ω resistor.
parts.listen: Two 6L6s into two tens break up earlier than a Twin Reverb but much later than a Princeton.
parts.together: Grid stoppers are 1500 Ω and screen resistors 470 Ω, 1 W, the same values as the tweed Twin. The rectifier is a GZ34 at 315 V AC.
parts.detail: This print is a later drawing. The first-year AA864 circuit wasn’t found and could differ in the bias arrangement.
sources: Fender "Vibrolux Reverb-Amp AA964" schematic, drawing J-FD

parts.label: Two tens at 4 ohms
parts.title: Two tens, wired for 4 ohms.
parts.body: Two ten-inch speakers make a 4-ohm load. Mojotone lists Jensen C10Q or Oxford 10L5 as stock. The cabinet is about 18 inches tall and 25 wide, with chrome glides and corners.
parts.listen: It’s a lot easier to carry than a Super Reverb or a Twin.
parts.together: The back panel carries the ground switch, fuse, power and standby switches, speaker and extension speaker jacks, and the pedal and reverb jacks.
parts.detail: Mojotone lists no logo for 1964 amps, but both dated first-year amps we found have one.
sources: Mojotone field guide: Blackface Vibrolux Reverb
